title: The Cardan grille approach to the Voynich MS taken to the next level
summary: Zandbergen recasts the table-and-grille procedure as a special case of combining fragments from three independent wheels. The paper calculates the resulting word-length distributions for several choices of fragment lengths and discusses how such wheels could produce meaningless text or encode information.
established: Tables 3–6 enumerate three 24-entry wheels. When the slots have binomial length counts in the ratio 1:3:3:1, selecting one entry from each wheel yields a shifted binomial distribution over total lengths 1–10. Two non-binomial examples in the same tables give approximate matches.

The construction gives neighbors by changing one fragment while holding the others fixed. The paper identifies the special behavior of f and p and the tokens outside Stolfi's word grammar as problems for a full manuscript account.

open.question: Can a compact, prespecified bank of fragment wheels retain the length and edit-distance patterns while explaining tokens that fall outside the proposed word grammar?
open.check: Freeze the wheel inventories and separator treatment on public training pages. Compare matched-size word-length and near-neighbor distributions and report the coverage of tokens outside the original grammar under both ZL and Takahashi.
